enonce_intro_markdown:
A discrete random variable $X$ has the following distribution.

| $x$ | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $P(X = x)$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ | $c$ | $\frac{3}{10}$ | $k$ | $\frac{3}{20}$ |
incertitudes: Question 3 : les points imprimés par partie, 5, 3 et 5, totalisent 13 ; recopiés tels quels. Les valeurs $c = \frac{1}{4}$ et $k = \frac{1}{10}$ sont cohérentes avec l'espérance $\frac{11}{4}$ imprimée en (b) (vérification faite).

questions.enonce_markdown: (a) Given that $P(X \le 2) = \frac{9}{11} P(X > 2)$, find the values of the probabilities $c$ and $k$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Condition 1: the probabilities sum to 1.**

$$\frac{1}{5} + c + \frac{3}{10} + k + \frac{3}{20} = 1 \;\Longrightarrow\; c + k = 1 - \frac{13}{20} = \frac{7}{20}$$

**Condition 2: the given relation.** $P(X \le 2) = \dfrac{1}{5} + c$ and $P(X > 2) = \dfrac{3}{10} + k + \dfrac{3}{20} = \dfrac{9}{20} + k$. Hence

$$\frac{1}{5} + c = \frac{9}{11}\left(\frac{9}{20} + k\right)$$

Substitute $k = \dfrac{7}{20} - c$, so $\dfrac{9}{20} + k = \dfrac{16}{20} - c = \dfrac{4}{5} - c$:

$$\frac{1}{5} + c = \frac{9}{11}\left(\frac{4}{5} - c\right)$$

Multiply by $55$:

$$11 + 55c = 36 - 45c \;\Longrightarrow\; 100c = 25 \;\Longrightarrow\; c = \frac{1}{4}$$

Then $k = \dfrac{7}{20} - \dfrac{5}{20} = \dfrac{2}{20} = \dfrac{1}{10}$.

**Check.** $P(X \le 2) = \dfrac{1}{5} + \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{9}{20}$ and $P(X > 2) = \dfrac{3}{10} + \dfrac{1}{10} + \dfrac{3}{20} = \dfrac{11}{20}$; $\dfrac{9}{11} \times \dfrac{11}{20} = \dfrac{9}{20}$ (true), and the five probabilities $\dfrac{4}{20}, \dfrac{5}{20}, \dfrac{6}{20}, \dfrac{2}{20}, \dfrac{3}{20}$ sum to $1$ (true).

**$c = \dfrac{1}{4}$ and $k = \dfrac{1}{10}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) Show that the expectation of $X$ is $\frac{11}{4}$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The expectation of a discrete random variable is $E(X) = \sum x\, P(X = x)$. With the probabilities $\dfrac{4}{20}, \dfrac{5}{20}, \dfrac{6}{20}, \dfrac{2}{20}, \dfrac{3}{20}$:

$$E(X) = 1 \times \frac{4}{20} + 2 \times \frac{5}{20} + 3 \times \frac{6}{20} + 4 \times \frac{2}{20} + 5 \times \frac{3}{20} = \frac{4 + 10 + 18 + 8 + 15}{20} = \frac{55}{20} = \frac{11}{4}$$

Hence $E(X) = \dfrac{11}{4}$, as required.
